t: You're looking at the Imperial Camel Corps Memorial, an outdoor sculpture in Victoria Embankment Gardens, on the Thames Embankment just east of Charing Cross station. It commemorates the Imperial Camel Corps, a unit of mounted infantry created in December 1916 from troops who had served in the Gallipoli campaign in the Dardanelles. The sculptor was Cecil Brown, a Scottish artist who lived from 1868 to 1926, and he made the memorial. It's a rather unexpected sight in a London garden beside the river.
